items.headline: A view on inflation is increasingly important
items.summary: The Fed has set out to tackle inflation and they certainly have the tools to get the job done. How aggressively they use those tools and how the economy responds is less certain, so is the geopolitical backdrop. At the moment, the market is pricing in the thinnest rate hike in US history so the consensus is that inflation will be tamed relatively easily. I think it's worth considering how much work needs to be done on inflation and what are the driving factors behind it. items.headline: What are the main events for today?
items.summary: EUROPEAN SESSION In the European session, we have the BoE rate decision. The central bank is expected to keep the Bank Rate unchanged at 3.75% with a 6-3 vote split, while keeping a tigthening bias. The BoE has enough reasons to stay put for now, following a soft UK employment report and benign inflation data. The market is pricing in 42 bps of tightening by year-end and a total of 102 bps by the end of 2027 (four rate hikes). AMERICAN SESSION In the American session, we get the latest US Jobless Claims figures. Initial Claims are expected at 206K vs 206K prior, while Continuing Claims are seen at 1779K vs 1774K prior. We will likely need a significant spike to the upside in initial claims to trigger a market reaction, as the labour market data has been stable for several months.
